[TODAY] 9,500 full Moons of sky, a billion-plus objects. 🌌

On Nov 12, ESA's Euclid space telescope released its first major data batch, called DR1-Foundation: about 13 months of observations with more than 900 million galaxies, over 60 million quasar candidates and around 15,000 strong gravitational lens candidates. Those lenses are galaxies whose gravity bends light from more distant ones. ESA says this catalog is bigger than all earlier ones combined.

Reality check: this covers only about 14% of the sky Euclid plans to survey. The full first release, with weak-lensing data, is due in mid-2027.

Save this if you want to follow how the dark universe gets mapped.

[TODAY] Could a DNA shot mean fewer throat surgeries?

In recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), HPV causes wart-like airway growths, often on the vocal cords. Surgery removes them, but they return. On Oct 30, the FDA granted accelerated approval to Voceryq, the first plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy in the U.S. Small loops of DNA, delivered with brief electrical pulses, help the immune system attack infected cells.

In its trial, 7 of 26 adults who had needed at least three surgeries the year before needed none in the first year after treatment.

Reality check: a small trial. A confirmatory study must still verify the benefit. This is research news, not medical advice.

Sources (link in bio):
U.S. FDA, Oct 30, 2026, "FDA Approves First Plasmid DNA-based Immunotherapy for Adults with Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis"

[TODAY] Roughly 1,000 km wide. Found only this October. 🪐

An icy world called 2026 ED138 was spotted on Oct 13 in data from the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. It sits about 46 au from the Sun, meaning 46 times Earth's distance (Pluto averages about 40). The team then found it in older survey images going back to 2016. It hid against the Milky Way's crowded stars. A Rubin team lead calls it the largest object of its kind found beyond Neptune in about 20 years.

Reality check: its size estimate spans 600 to 1,500 km. More observations must show it is round before it can join the five recognized dwarf planets.

[EMERGING] Use a quantum computer you don't trust?

Most people will reach quantum computers over the internet, owned by someone else. A new preprint by researchers at MIT, UIUC and NTT Research shows on paper how an ordinary computer could use one untrusted quantum server as if it were its own. The server does the work but cannot read the computation. Attempts to cheat can be caught. Think of a sealed envelope that gets processed without being opened.

Reality check: this is theory, not a running system. It relies on a math problem believed to resist quantum attacks. It has not yet been peer reviewed. Reports note heavy data traffic.

Would you rent quantum time from a stranger? Tell us below.

[IMAGINE] A planet hid in two-year-old Webb images. 🔭

What is real: planets can be a million times fainter than their stars. Leftover glare buries them. A Northwestern-led team built a digital twin of the James Webb Space Telescope, tuned it to match each observation and then subtracted the simulated glare. In Nature, they report faint planets became 2 to 15 times easier to detect. The giant planet 51 Eridani b emerged in old Webb data where standard processing had missed it.

Reality check: that planet was already known from ground telescopes, so this is a recovery, not a new find.

The speculation: what if telescope archives already hold worlds nobody has seen?
